out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: - OBSERVED: half-half stored in a pitcher at espresso station was not labeled with 4 hour end point.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to-eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated CFM and CFM labeled the half-half with 4 hour end point.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. - OBSERVED: a food employee failed to wash hands and change gloves after cracking eggs and before cooking.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated the CFM and food employee.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitizing, Contact Time Met
violations.observation: Chemical sanitizer immersion time was not adequate for @SANITIZING AGENTS@ sanitizing solution. - OBSERVED: a food employee dipped a salad bowl in chlorine solution in sanitizing basin at 3-compartment sink and took it out immediately.
violations.corrective_action: Chemical sanitization (manual or mechanical operations) including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods using a solution by providing: 1) an exposure time of at least 10 seconds for a chlorine solution, 2) an exposure time of at least 7 seconds for a chlorine solution of 50mg/L that has a pH of 10 or less and a water temperature of 100F or a pH of 8 or less and a water temperature of 75F, 3) an exposure time of at least 30 seconds for other chemical sanitizing solutions, or 4) an exposure time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and pH that when evaluated for efficacy yields sanitization. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated the CFM and food employees.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the chlorine-based sanitizing solution was observed to be at a concentration less than what is required for effective sanitization of food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils. Observed the sanitizing solution in the @LOCATION@ with a concentration of @NUMBER@ ppm total chlorine. - OBSERVED: (1) chlorine solution in a sanitizer bucket was much higher than 200ppm; (2) chlorine solution in the sanitizing basin at 3-compartment sink was less than 50ppm.
violations.corrective_action: A chlorine-based sanitizing solution shall have a minimum concentration of at least 50 to 200 ppm total chlorine when tested using the appropriate test kit. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated the CFM and food employees; CFM adjusted the concentration of chlorine solution to 50-200ppm.

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment were not observed sanitized: - OBSERVED: a food employee rinsed a salad bowl at prep sink and stored on storage rack for clean utensils for future use.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated the CFM and food employees. Salad bowl was sent to wash.

violations.title: (2017) Non-Continuous Cooking Process
violations.observation: The following raw animal foods were not properly cooked using a non-continuous cooking process: - OBSERVED: general Tso chicken (86f) and chicken (113-118f) were not fully cooked and stored in hot holding box for about 1 hour.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods that were cooked using a non-continuous cook process shall be subject to an initial heating process that is no longer than 60 minutes in duration; immediately, after initial heating, cooled according to the time and temperature parameters specified for cooked time/temperature control for safety food; after cooling, held frozenor cold; prior to sale or service, cooked using a process that heats all parts of the food to a temperature and for a time as specified under 3-401.11A-C; Cooled according to the time and temperature parameters specified under 3-501.14A if not hot held, served immediately or held using time as a public health control. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated the CFM and discussed non-continuous cooking process. General Tso chicken was cooked to 212f and chicken was cooked to 182f. GREENSBORO CAFE (Inspection Date: 04/07/2026) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. - OBSERVED: grilled chicken (43f-45f) was stored in M3 3-door upright cooler overnight.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated CFM. CFM discarded the food item.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: - OBSERVED: general Tso chicken (86f) and chicken (113-118f) were stored in hot box for about 1 hour.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated CFM. General Tso chicken was cooked to 212f, and chicken was cooked to 182f.

violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is commercially processed is not used or discarded within 24 hours of when the original container was opened and is not observed to be date marked: - OBSERVED: mixed cheddar cheese and Monterey Jack cheese opened one day prior to the inspection was not properly labeled with date.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: CFM properly marked the food item.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): half-half stored in a pitcher at espresso station.
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: EHS educated CFM. Time as a public health control procedure has been established.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: - OBSERVED: squeeze bottles of chipotle sauce, ranch sauce, and sour cream stored in M3 prep cooler were not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: CFM labeled the squeeze bottles properly.

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: CFM provided hair restraints.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Plumbing connections under the hand sink next to M3 2-door upright cooler are leaking.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: The hand sink basin next to 3-compartment sink was slow to drain.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. - CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: CFM unclogged the hand sink. GREENSBORO CAFE (Inspection Date: 04/07/2026) Page 3 of 4

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: (1) SLICED HAM (40F) WAS PREPARED ON 10/8/2025. HOWEVER, IT WAS MARKED WITH PREPARATION DATE OF 10/9/2025. (2) COOKED CHICKEN (41F) WAS PREPARED ON 10/8/2025. HOWEVER IS WAS LABELED WITH PREPARATION DATE OF 10/4/2025.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. CFM CORRECTED THE VIOLATIONS..

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: BULKY VOLUME OF CUT LETTUCE (64F) WAS PACKED AND STORED IN A BIG CONTAINER IN M3 3-DOOR UPRIGHT COOLER FOR 2 HOURS.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CFM STORED THE CUT LETTUCE IN TWO CONTAINERS.
